The '''2011 [[Tippeligaen]]''' was the 67th completed season of top division [[association football|football]] in [[Norway]]. The competition began on 20 March 2011 and ended on 27 November 2011. [[Rosenborg BK|Rosenborg]] were the defending champions, having secured their twenty-second [[Norwegian football league champions|League Championship]] on 24 October 2010.<ref name="Burheim">{{cite news|url=http://www.dagbladet.no/2010/10/24/sport/fotball/tippeligaen/rosenborg/tromso/13988329/|title=- I kveld skal vi feire|last=Burheim|first=Mads Gudim|date=2010-10-24|publisher=[[Dagbladet]]|language=no|access-date=2010-10-24| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20101025211216/http://www.dagbladet.no/2010/10/24/sport/fotball/tippeligaen/rosenborg/tromso/13988329/| archive-date= 25 October 2010 | url-status= live}}</ref> [[Sogndal Fotball|Sogndal]], [[Sarpsborg 08 FF|Sarpsborg 08]] and [[Fredrikstad FK|Fredrikstad]] entered as the three promoted teams from the [[2010 1. divisjon]]. They replaced [[Hønefoss BK|Hønefoss]], [[Kongsvinger IL Toppfotball|Kongsvinger]] and [[Sandefjord Fotball|Sandefjord]] who were relegated to the [[2011 1. divisjon]].

[[Molde FK|Molde]] won their first ever Eliteserien title with two games to spare. Molde's 58 points was a record low for an Eliteserien champion in the current 16-team system.<ref name="Tables">{{cite web |url=https://www.fotballen.eu/Emner/Tippeligaen_statistikk.html |title=Statistikk for den norske Eliteserien |language=no |access-date=26 June 2018 |archive-date=1 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190301105139/https://www.fotballen.eu/Emner/Tippeligaen_statistikk.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> 

The fastest goal in Norwegian top division history was scored this season on 15 April by [[Erik Mjelde]] in a 3–3 draw between his side [[SK Brann|Brann]] and [[FK Haugesund|Haugesund]] after 11 seconds.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vg.no/sport/fotball/i/lBJ69/det-er-mulig-aa-score-enda-raskere-enn-mjelde |title=- Det er mulig å score enda raskere enn Mjelde|trans-title=- It is possible to score even faster than Mjelde|date=17 April 2011|access-date=10 October 2018 |language=no |publisher=Verdens Gang |work=vg.no }}</ref>

==Overview==
At the end of the season, [[Sarpsborg 08 FF|Sarpsborg 08]] and [[IK Start|Start]] were relegated to the [[2012 1. divisjon]], due to having finished in the bottom two positions in the standings. There was no two-legged promotion play-offs this season.

On 30 October 2011, [[Molde FK|Molde]] became champions with two games to spare after their only remaining challenger, [[Rosenborg BK|Rosenborg]], lost 3–6 to [[SK Brann|Brann]] in the 28th round of the series. The trophy was their first ever league championship.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.vg.no/sport/fotball/norsk/artikkel.php?artid=10023251|title = Molde-kaptein Berg Hestad varsler vill gullfeiring}}</ref>

==Teams==
Sixteen teams competed in the league – the top thirteen teams from the previous season, and the three teams promoted from [[2010 1. divisjon|1. divisjon]]. The promoted teams were [[Sogndal Fotball|Sogndal]], [[Sarpsborg 08 FF|Sarpsborg 08]] and [[Fredrikstad FK|Fredrikstad]]. This was Sarpsborg 08's first top-flight season, while Sogndal and Fredrikstad returned to the top flight after an absence of six years and one season respectively. They replaced [[Hønefoss BK|Hønefoss]] (returning after their debut season in the first tier), [[Kongsvinger IL Toppfotball|Kongsvinger]] (relegated after a season's presence) and [[Sandefjord Fotball|Sandefjord]] (relegated after two years in the top flight).
